test_title: PYST 28: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - Reasoning (Held On: 21th Sep 2025 Shift 1)
subject: reasoning
question: Comprehension: There are 7 family members: A, B, C, D, E, F and G going to a party. There are three generations in which only two are married couples. A is the grandfather of F who is a male. C is the son-in-law of D. G is the son of B. D has only two children, both of the same gender. E is the sister-in-law of C. How many males are there?
solution:
Decoding symbols for Family Tree:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/153c6a6e313de03f2911e6352e768c319ce48bd8d9b10cf6c7d58c07f604979a.png] 

Step-by-step Relationship Analysis:

 
• A is the grandfather of F
 
• C is the son-in-law of D. This means C (+) is married to D's daughter.
 
• D has only two children, both of the same gender. Since C is a son-in-law, both children of D must be female. 
 
• E is the sister-in-law of C. Since D's children are both female, E must be the sister of C's wife. 
 
• Since there are only two married couples, and A is a grandfather, A must be married to D.
 
• B must be the wife of C and the daughter of A and D. 
 
• G is the son of B.
 
• Since B and C are married, G and F are siblings or cousins. In a 7-member tree, F and G are the third generation.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**
